govdocs-archive_org-ShatteringTheAbraham: The old Review’s Lincoln-icon smasher takes the other view of the rail-splitter. The hot article fits the other-side shelf. Lincoln scholars answer it point by point. Read it with both eyes open. Set it by the standard lives. Its sayings are hotly fought over.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agonistici: This 1913 reference piece on the Agonistici — the Donatist fighters, also called Circumcellions — tells their wild tale. John Joseph A'Becket follows their raids. They scared Catholic Africa with clubs and cries. Men seeking death roamed the fields. Augustine's pen at last wore them down.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amerigo-vespu: This 1913 reference piece on Amerigo Vespucci — the Florentine who gave America its name. Gustavo Uzielli weighs his voyages. His letters spread the New World's fame. Two continents bear his Christian name. The mapmaker's immortal namesake. His name was a publisher's happy thought.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolici: This 1913 reference article on the Apostolici — the heretical sect of the Apostolic Brethren. John Joseph A'Becket tells their wild tale. Segarelli's followers defied the Church. The Inquisition ended their dream. A sect of the thirteenth century. Their penance was public and severe.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arabici: This 1913 reference piece on the Arabici — the heretics of the sleeping soul. Francis Havey notes their third-century error. They denied the soul's waking death. Origen convinced them of their fault. A heresy that yielded to reason. Their sleep ended at the judgment.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolommeo-a: This 1913 reference piece on the Carducci brothers — Bartolommeo and Vincenzo, painters. George Williamson notes their works. The entry preserves their modest fame. Their brushes served the Spanish court. Artists of the seventeenth century. Their altarpieces grace the Escorial. Their frescoes adorn the Buen Retiro.
